content.title: About
content.content: Basbousa is a traditional Middle Eastern dessert consisting of a syrup‑soaked cake made from semolina, butter and sugar. The batter often includes nuts, coconut flakes or flavorings such as rose water or orange zest.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The name comes from the Arabic word “basbousa”, meaning “soft” or “fluffy”.
It is traditionally baked in square or diamond pans and topped with nuts or coconut.
Regional variations exist: Egyptian versions may use yogurt, while Turkish ones often add pistachios.
Basbousa is commonly served during holidays like Ramadan and Eid al‑Fitr.
The soaking syrup can be scented with rose water, orange blossom water (attar), or mint.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rich in carbohydrates and fats, basbousa provides a quick boost of energy, useful during fasting periods.

items.title: Calcium content
items.content: Butter and occasional dairy additions make the dessert a decent source of calcium for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Semolina supplies B1 and B2 vitamins, which support metabolic processes.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Flavorings like rose water contain flavonoids that act as antioxidants.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Because it is sweet, people with diabetes or those watching their weight should consume basbousa in moderation.

items.title: Nut allergy
items.content: If nuts are included, they may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Butter adds saturated fat, which can affect cholesterol levels if eaten frequently.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Basbousa is served at room temperature, often alongside tea or coffee. Cut into bite‑size pieces, garnish with nuts, coconut, or fresh berries. Leftovers keep in the fridge and are best eaten within 2–3 days.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store basbousa in an airtight container in the refrigerator. For longer keeping, it can be frozen for up to 2 months after portioning.
